subject: Next steps: reserve dedicated pool slot + throughput checklist
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Maya Li <maya@starpay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps to lock a dedicated pool slot

Thanks again for taking time today, Maya — great conversation. Quick recap and a proposed next step so we can lock time and capacity for Starpay's proof-of-concept.

Summary of today's discovery
- Primary workload: document-to-invoice extraction + real-time transaction summarization for fraud signals.
- Target latency SLO: 150-250ms p95 on generation paths, burst tolerances to ~120 concurrent streams.
- Expected steady-state tokens: ~4M tokens/day, with daily peaks up to 9M.
- Security: VPC peering preferred; data retention window 30 days.

Ask / next step
1) Schedule a 90-minute dedicated capacity sizing deep-dive where Ben will run an intake of load profile and we’ll model GPU pool sizing + batching options.
2) Please attach a representative 1-hour load sample or CSV export of request rates (timestamps + avg tokens) before the call.

I attached a short Redwood sizing checklist to help collect the items Ben will need. Proposed slots (PST):
- Tue Feb 17 10:00–11:30
- Tue Feb 17 14:00–15:30
- Wed Feb 18 09:00–10:30

Can you confirm which works for your team? If none, send a few options and we’ll match.

Thanks,
Priya Naranajan (Priya)
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Priya@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-sizing-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet, 10KB)
From: Maya Li <maya@starpay.com>
To: Priya Naranajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: ops+infra@starpay.com
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 08:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps to lock a dedicated pool slot

Priya — thanks for the clear recap. 14:00–15:30 PST on Tue Feb 17 works for our infra and product folks.

I attached a brief CSV with a 60-min sample from last Tuesday (timestamps + requests/min + avg prompt tokens). High level numbers:
- steady 120 reqs/min, peak bursts ~480 reqs/min for ~6 minutes
- avg input tokens 360, avg output tokens 80

We also have an internal constraint: sessions must fail open to smaller models if an SLA tier is exceeded — worth a quick note during sizing. We'll bring our infra lead (Sam Chen) and product manager (Aisha K.) to the call.

Thanks,
Maya Li
VP, Product
Starpay

Attachment: starpay-load-description.csv (text/csv, 3KB)

Perfect — locking Tue 17 14:00–15:30 PST. I sent a calendar invite (link below) to all listed.

Pre-call homework for productive sizing session
- Ben: I’ll lead the throughput modeling, focusing on batching/kv cache strategy and fallbacks to model variants.
- Maya / Starpay: If you can confirm peak concurrent stream count and whether inference is telecom (real-time streaming) vs batch for the summarization path, that’ll help us choose pooling config.
- Bring any SLA language you expect (p95 p99 targets) and any compliance notes for VPC peering.

Who should own the shared baseline test we’ll run during the session? If Starpay provides a small replay script that mimics the CSV sample, Ben can run it against a sandbox pool. If you prefer, we can prepare replay on our side — we’d just need an API key-scoped test token.

Calendar invite: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=starpay-sizing-20260217
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/98765

Thanks — see you tomorrow,
Priya

Thanks, team — I’ll prep the sizing workbook and a short checklist of tests we'll run in the session. Quick notes ahead of the call:
- If bursts hit ~480 reqs/min with 360/80 tokens, we'll look at a combination of 2x smaller model variants for fallback + a dedicated pool sized for sustained 120 reqs/min with burst capacity to 500 for short windows.
- Bring any constraints on acceptable model quantizations (e.g., no int8 if you require bit-exact outputs).
- I’ll drop a pre-read in the HubSpot record and attach the workbook to the calendar event.
